page.title: Accounts
page.description: Where your money sits, and how much of it sits where.

empty.title: No accounts yet
empty.description: Add your first account to start tracking balances and linking transactions.

retired.heading: Inactive
retired.description: These accounts are hidden from your dashboard and left out of your totals. Their transactions are untouched, and you can still filter by them anywhere in the app.

deactivateDialog.title: Deactivate {{name}}?
deactivateDialog.description: It disappears from your dashboard and stops counting towards your balances. Nothing is deleted — its transactions stay, and you can still filter by it. Reactivate it any time.

deleteDialog.title: Delete {{name}}?
deleteDialog.description: Transactions recorded against this account are removed with it. This cannot be undone. To hide it without losing anything, deactivate it instead.

toasts.deleteFailed: Could not delete the account. Try again.
toasts.deactivated: Account deactivated — find it under Inactive
toasts.activeChangeFailed: Could not change the account. Try again.

form.description: The card below is exactly how it will look on the Accounts page.
form.balanceHint: Use a negative value for credit cards with outstanding balance.
form.providerSyncedNote: Balance, type and currency are managed automatically by the {{provider}} sync — edit them from the Investments page.

apiKeys.title: API Keys
apiKeys.description: Create keys so scripts and integrations can use your data. Each key is shown only once.
apiKeys.nameEachKey: Name each key after what uses it.
apiKeys.empty: No API keys yet. Create one to get started — see the guide below for what it can do.
apiKeys.createDescription: Give it a name and choose what it is allowed to do.
apiKeys.name: Name
apiKeys.nameHelp: So you know which integration uses it.
apiKeys.readOnlyHelp: Can only fetch data (GET). Safest for dashboards.
apiKeys.fullAccessHelp: Can also create, edit and delete your data.
apiKeys.createdWarning: This key will not be shown again — only a hash is stored.
apiKeys.copyFailed: Could not copy — select the text and copy manually
apiKeys.revokeDescription: Anything using this key stops working immediately. This cannot be undone.
apiKeys.guideTitle: What you can do with API keys
apiKeys.guideDescription: An API key lets a script, spreadsheet or dashboard read (and optionally change) your data without your password.
apiKeys.authTextSuffix: header on every request. All endpoints live under
apiKeys.readOnlyForbidden: Requests that would change data are rejected with
apiKeys.readOnlyUse: Use these for dashboards and reporting.
apiKeys.fullAccessDetails: keys can also create, edit and delete
apiKeys.fullAccessAsYou: as you, on your own data.
apiKeys.cannotManageKeys: Keys cannot create or revoke other keys; you must be signed in for that.
apiKeys.revokeImmediate: Revoking a key stops it working immediately.
apiKeys.endpointsFooter: This is a short overview. The full interactive list, with request and response shapes, is at
apiKeys.safetyPassword: Treat a key like a password — don't commit it to git or paste it into chats.
apiKeys.safetyOneKey: Create one key per integration, so you can revoke just the one that leaks.
apiKeys.safetyReadOnly: Prefer read-only unless the integration really needs to write.
